title: Allow development packages to install locked backends
description:
## Summary

- Validate downloaded backend metadata against the artifact package version recorded in the backend catalog.
- Record that version when packaging and merging complete and CPU-only backend catalogs.
- Add regression coverage for installing a released backend from a development package.

## Public-facing changes

Development package versions such as `0.4.0.9000` can install the prebuilt GPU and CPU backends pinned by their catalogs. Archive hashes, backend hashes, R versions, platforms, dependency versions, and source commits remain validated.

## Internal changes

Backend catalogs now include a `package_version` column. The cross-version model-state test now uses explicit released-version provenance instead of relying on the frozen fixture version differing from the current package version.

## Testing

- `CUDA_ML_GPU_TESTS=false Rscript -e 'devtools::test(reporter = "summary")'`
- `CUDA_ML_GPU_TESTS=false CUDA_ML_CPU_RUNTIME_TESTS=true Rscript -e 'devtools::test(filter = "runtime-functional", reporter = "summary")'`
- Clean-cache CPU backend installation and audit from package version `0.4.0.9000`
- `R CMD check --as-cran --no-manual`: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes

title: Replace iris examples and test fixtures
description:
## Summary

- Replace deprecated iris examples across the public documentation with compact datasets from modeldata, and use Old Faithful for the release post's concise k-means demonstration.
- Replace the internal iris-based GPU test fixture with Palmer penguins, preserving coverage for multiclass modeling, clustering, serialization, and dimensionality reduction.
- Update the tidymodels examples to use current native-pipe APIs, add the optional dataset dependencies, and regenerate the README, function reference, vignettes, and pkgdown site.

## Public-facing changes

All user-facing examples now avoid iris and use complete datasets without missing-value cleanup. The release post keeps installation focused on cuda.ml and assumes optional example packages are available. Other documentation uses ordinary numeric literals and `set.seed()` where reproducibility matters.

## Internal changes

GPU tests use a shared, scaled Palmer penguins fixture. Dataset-dependent assertions now account for component-sign ambiguity and compare clustering quality using inertia and adjusted Rand index. There are no public API changes.

## Testing

- `Rscript -e 'devtools::test(reporter = "progress")'` (424 passed, 9 skipped)
- `R CMD build /home/tomasz/github/mlverse/cuda.ml`
- `_R_CHECK_CRAN_INCOMING_=false _R_CHECK_SYSTEM_CLOCK_=false R CMD check --no-manual --as-cran cuda.ml_0.4.0.tar.gz` (`Status: OK`)
- `Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("README.Rmd")'`
- `Rscript -e 'pkgdown::build_site()'`
- Rendered the Old Faithful k-means plot with Quarto against the GPU backend.

title: Clean up rendered documentation output
description:
## Summary

- Remove the redundant printed label from the README confusion-matrix example.
- Hide the bare `NULL` result from the model-persistence save example.
- Regenerate the tracked pkgdown, LLM, and search artifacts.

## Root cause

The README uses collapsed chunk output, so the `cat()` result appeared before the source expression that produced the matrix. The model-persistence save call also exposed its otherwise uninformative `NULL` result during rendering.

## Impact

The public documentation renders each result beside the expression that produced it and omits an unhelpful serialization result. There are no public API or internal runtime changes.

## Validation

- Rendered `README.Rmd` with rmarkdown.
- Rebuilt the pkgdown home page and model-persistence article, including LLM and search exports.
- Ran documentation output assertions and `git diff --check`.

title: Modernize R examples and tidymodels guidance
description:
## Summary

Modernize user-facing examples and generated documentation for the refreshed cuda.ml interface.

- replace magrittr pipes with base R pipes and purrr formula lambdas with base anonymous functions
- update the recipe example to use a tidymodels workflow and document the current case-weight boundary
- enable roxygen Markdown so lists, code, and links render correctly
- regenerate the README, reference documentation, and pkgdown site
- remove the unused magrittr suggestion and correct existing dependency minimums

## Public-facing changes

Examples now show modern R syntax and the recommended tidymodels workflow pattern. Reference pages now render their existing Markdown correctly.

No exported functions or runtime behavior changed.

## Internal changes

Tests now use base pipes and anonymous functions and avoid superseded purrr flattening helpers. Dependency metadata now matches APIs already used by the package.

title: Add the 0.4.2 backend release catalogs
description:
## Summary

- update the complete CUDA/RAPIDS backend catalog to the artifacts built from merge commit `d427cd0`
- refresh the CPU-only nvForest backend catalog from the same source for R 4.1 through R 4.6
- point both catalogs at the draft `cuda-ml-backend-0.4.2` release

## Public-facing changes

After the draft release is published, `cuda_ml_install()` can resolve backend revision 0.4.2 for every supported R minor. The complete backend contains the PCA and TSVD batch-dimension fix merged in PR #221. CPU-only nvForest installations resolve the corresponding 0.4.2 artifacts built from the same source commit.

The release remains a draft while this PR is open, so these catalog URLs are not yet available to unauthenticated package installations.

## Internal changes

This PR changes only the two generated catalog TSV files. It does not change R code, native code, build tooling, or workflows.

Each catalog contains six rows covering R 4.1 through R 4.6. The rows record the generated filenames, 0.4.2 release URLs, byte sizes, archive SHA-256 values, and backend binary SHA-256 values. The package version remains 0.4.0 in artifact filenames because backend release revisions are versioned separately.

## Validation

- backend workflow run 31018956949 passed all six R-version builds and the draft-release job at `d427cd0`
- the committed catalogs match the generated `backend-lock` artifact byte-for-byte
- `Rscript -e 'devtools::test(filter = "runtime-loader", reporter = "summary")'`
- `git diff --check`

## Release sequencing

Keep `cuda-ml-backend-0.4.2` as a draft until this PR merges. Publish the release after both catalogs are present on `main`.

title: Finalize the cuda.ml 0.4.0 release
description:
## Summary

- Rewrite the 0.4.0 NEWS entry for users moving from the released 0.3 API and for first-time users.
- Simplify the README, installation guide, persistence documentation, and function reference, then rebuild the package website.
- Add a release blog draft and evaluate the parsnip and persistence guides when building the GPU documentation path.

## Public-facing changes

- Document the exported-symbol and signature changes found by comparing v0.3.3 with this branch, including the installer, nvForest replacement, random-forest and regression APIs, preprocessing, logging, prediction, and removed upstream interfaces.
- Add gzip-compressed file paths to `cuda_ml_serialize()` and `cuda_ml_unserialize()`. Open connections and uncompressed raw vectors remain supported.
- Document the supported persistence families, bundle and fresh-process workflows, restore-device behavior, and the specific reasons KNN and TSVD fits are not yet supported.
- Clarify the separate contracts for backend inspection and runtime auditing, the roles of the approximate-KNN constructors, and the distinction between prediction and dimensionality-reduction transforms.
- Remove the README's single-GPU limitations column, add Tomasz Kalinowski to the package reference authors, and explain the distinction between binary-backend tags and R package releases in the installation guide.

## Internal changes

- Remove compatibility branches for unreleased intermediate nvForest and random-forest state classes and use one canonical state class per family.
- Add a reusable released-API signature comparison script.
- Add public-API coverage for compressed path persistence and for selecting and restoring an nvForest model on the second visible GPU.

## Testing

- `Rscript -e 'devtools::test(reporter = "summary")'`
- `Rscript -e 'devtools::test(filter = "nvforest-state", reporter = "summary")'`
- GPU-evaluated `pkgdown::build_site()` with the parsnip and persistence vignettes rendered
- `R CMD build .`
- `R CMD check --no-manual cuda.ml_0.4.0.tar.gz` — Status: OK

Users can now navigate the reference by task and follow focused guides for setup, modeling, persistence, and deployment. Corrected help text and examples are included in the rebuilt site.

The MNIST render now requires local inputs with pinned SHA-256 checksums before the existing loader runs, so rendering cannot fall through to its network download path. K-means and UMAP use explicit seeds, while the SVM sample split retains its explicit R seed.

title: Complete nvForest persistence, interchange, and CPU deployment
description:
## Summary

- complete the nvForest public surface and verify every advertised input format
- make nvForest and cuML random-forest persistence device neutral, and add a standard Treelite checkpoint plus cuda.ml JSON round-trip
- add a separate CPU-only nvForest backend that avoids the complete CUDA and RAPIDS runtime

## Public-facing changes

nvForest is now the common inference layer for random forests trained by cuda.ml and tree ensembles exported by XGBoost, LightGBM, or Treelite. cuda.ml trains its random-forest path with cuML on a GPU; it does not train XGBoost or LightGBM models. GPU inference is the accelerated path for imported ensembles, while CPU inference provides a compatible deployment path on hosts without a GPU.

`cuda_ml_serialize()` writes v2 device-neutral states for nvForest and `cuda_ml_rand_forest()` models. `cuda_ml_unserialize()` accepts restore-time `device`, `device_id`, `layout`, `precision`, `default_chunk_size`, and `align_bytes` settings; GPU remains the default. Legacy nvForest states remain supported with their saved inference settings. `bundle::bundle()` remains optional and can bind an nvForest model to a deployment device separately from its nested state.

`cuda_ml_nvforest_export()` writes `<prefix>.treelite.checkpoint` and `<prefix>.cuda-ml.json` to a caller-supplied directory. The checkpoint is independently loadable as a standard Treelite checkpoint. The JSON sidecar binds the pair by size and SHA-256 and retains cuda.ml ABI and compatibility metadata, class labels, prediction precision, random-forest probability semantics, processed feature names when available, and the R preprocessing blueprint. `cuda_ml_nvforest_import()` validates the pair and restores the full cuda.ml model on a caller-selected device. The sidecar contains R serialization and therefore has the same trusted-artifact boundary as `readRDS()` and `cuda_ml_unserialize()`.

`cuda_ml_install(device = "cpu")` installs only the nvForest CPU inference backend. It is roughly 1 MiB compressed and 3 MiB installed, requires no GPU or NVIDIA driver, and contains no CUDA or RAPIDS shared runtime. The complete roughly 1.6 GiB backend remains necessary for cuML training and GPU inference, and continues to support nvForest CPU inference when it is already installed.

The offline vignette covers GPU training followed by CPU-only deployment, the checkpoint-pair workflow, XGBoost and LightGBM loading, CPU/GPU selection, regression, class and probability prediction, inspection, leaf IDs, per-tree output, both persistence forms, fresh-process restoration, and a Plumber-style service. It also states that per-tree results fully materialize `rows × trees × outputs` in R and that `chunk_size` does not bound result memory.

All five advertised formats have committed public-API fixtures with provenance and expected predictions: XGBoost UBJSON, JSON, legacy binary, LightGBM text, and Treelite checkpoint. The four documented suffix-inference paths are covered as well.

## Internal changes

The standalone CPU shared object compiles nvForest's CPU inference templates and statically links Treelite. Its archive contains only backend metadata, the shared object, and consolidated third-party license notices. Build and runtime audits verify archive contents, hashes, native registration, versions, dynamic dependencies, symbol visibility, and manylinux ABI limits.

Checkpoint-pair export and import require no additional native serialization format. They reuse the Treelite checkpoint bytes already produced by nvForest and reconstruct the existing v2 state contract so the exact Treelite compatibility gate remains authoritative.

The backend-release workflow builds complete and CPU-only artifacts for every supported R minor. CI exercises GPU training and inference, complete-runtime CPU inference, and the isolated slim CPU runtime independently.

## Testing

- all six hosted checks passed: offline R release and devel checks, native image build, slim CPU-only nvForest runtime, full-runtime CPU, and GPU
- network-disabled nvForest vignette render
- `R CMD build`, including vignette creation
- `R CMD check --no-manual` (`Status: OK`)
- focused nvForest tests: 58 passed locally
- full-backend CPU nvForest runtime tests: 22 passed in the native test image
- every advertised input format and documented suffix-inference path
- GPU-trained classifier export followed by fresh GPU-hidden CPU import with matching class and probability predictions
- transformed-formula random-forest regression round-trip with restored preprocessing and processed feature order
- checkpoint overwrite, independent Treelite loading, and checksum-mismatch rejection

## Release gate

The CPU backend catalog in this PR is intentionally header-only. After merge, run the `cuda-ml-backend-0.4.1` workflow from the merge commit, then land the generated full-backend and CPU-backend catalog rows in a focused follow-up. Do not publish the package until both catalogs reference the 0.4.1 assets.

title: Define durable model persistence compatibility
description:
## Summary

cuda.ml schema 1 model states now treat `package_version` as provenance instead of an unconditional restoration gate. Compatibility is determined by the state schema, the model ABI, and the backend identity required by that model family.

- Linear and logistic-regression states do not require matching backend identity fields.
- PCA, SVC, one-vs-rest SVC, SVR, and UMAP states require the recorded RAPIDS version.
- Random-forest and nvForest states require the recorded Treelite version.
- Unknown schemas and ABIs, missing payloads, and missing or incompatible required backend fields continue to fail with specific errors.

The tests include a frozen schema-1 linear state from a different package version. Pure-R and native-state models are also written to disk, restored in fresh R processes, and used for prediction through both `cuda_ml_unserialize()` and `bundle::unbundle()`.

## User-facing changes

Compatible models can be deployed across cuda.ml package-version changes. NEWS and the serialization and bundle documentation now state the exact schema-1 compatibility matrix and the absence of implicit migrations or native-pointer fallback behavior. No public API signatures changed.

## Internal changes

Model ABI identifiers are mapped to their required backend identity fields before S3 restoration. Other backend fields remain recorded provenance. No native sources or backend assets changed.

## Testing

- Focused model-state, SVM serialization, and nvForest runtime tests: 34 passed.
- `R CMD check --no-manual cuda.ml_0.4.0.tar.gz`: Status OK.

title: Remove dead IVFPQ argument
description:
## Summary

Remove the unsupported `use_precomputed_tables` argument from `cuda_ml_knn_algo_ivfpq()` and its generated documentation. The argument could only be `FALSE`, so it did not provide usable behavior with the cuVS backend.

Keep the native `usePrecomputedTables` parameter field and set it unconditionally to `FALSE` for ABI compatibility. Existing validation for `nlist`, `nprobe`, `m`, and `n_bits` is unchanged.

## Impact

The public IVFPQ constructor now accepts exactly `nlist`, `nprobe`, `m`, and `n_bits`. Supported IVFPQ calls retain their existing behavior. Native sources and backend artifacts are unchanged.

## Validation

- Confirmed the new signature regression test failed before implementation because the constructor exposed five formals.
- Ran the focused forward API tests: 64 passed and 2 environment-dependent tests skipped.
- Regenerated documentation with roxygen2 8.0.0 and rendered the generated IVFPQ Rd file successfully.
- Ran `R CMD check --no-manual --as-cran` from a tracked-files-only source export: `Status: OK`.

title: Publish the CUDA backend release catalog
description:
## Summary

The post-merge backend release run built all six archives, then failed while merging the catalog because `read.delim()` parsed R minor versions as numeric values. This change reads `r_version` as text and adds the generated catalog for R 4.1 through 4.6.

The verified archives and catalog are attached to the unpublished draft release `cuda-ml-backend-0.4.0`.

## Public-facing changes

- Adds the release catalog used by `cuda_ml_install()` to select the prebuilt backend for R 4.1 through 4.6.
- Records each archive's URL, size, archive SHA-256, and backend SHA-256.

## Internal changes

- Keeps R minor versions as character values when the release workflow merges per-build catalog rows.
- Does not change package APIs or native backend code.

## Validation

- Reproduced the catalog merge failure against the six artifacts from workflow run 30847456447, then reran the same command successfully after the fix.
- Validated all six archives against the generated catalog, including size, SHA-256, contents, embedded metadata, backend hash, platform, R version, and source commit.
- Installed cuda.ml 0.4.0 into an isolated library and prepared a clean managed runtime using the exact draft backend through a local mirror.
- Ran the managed-runtime functional tests and the CPU-only nvForest load, prediction, per-tree prediction, serialization, restoration, and bundle tests.
- Ran the full runtime audit and verified that reuse of the completed cache performs no network download.

title: Target RAPIDS 26.06 with a managed runtime, nvForest, and static Treelite
description:
## Summary

This is a breaking 0.4.0 release built around one supported backend contract: CUDA Toolkit 13.2.2, RAPIDS cuML and nvForest 26.06, and Treelite 4.7.0 on Ubuntu 26.04 x86_64.

The PR removes native compatibility paths for backend versions and capabilities that the package can no longer produce. It preserves R modeling conventions instead: hardhat inputs and blueprints, tidymodels parameter names and prediction columns, factor levels, recipes, and portable model bundling.

It also makes the functional R-universe binary self-provisioning from an R user's perspective. Users install the package, run `cuda_ml_install()` once to prepare the exact locked CUDA/RAPIDS/nvForest runtime, and then use the modeling APIs without installing CUDA, cuML, Python, conda, a compiler, or Treelite. Treelite 4.7.0 is linked statically into the package backend.

## Public-facing changes

- Adds an Ubuntu 26.04 x86_64 R-universe binary containing the compiled backend and a private static Treelite 4.7.0 build. `cuda_ml_install()` explicitly downloads approximately 1.6 GiB of locked CUDA/RAPIDS/nvForest archives; model operations never download them implicitly.
- Adds `cuda_ml_backend_info()` for non-provisioning backend and runtime metadata, `cuda_ml_runtime_audit()` for explicit integrity and dependency validation, and `cuda_ml_cache_clean()` for explicit cache removal. Package loading does not inspect the GPU, create a cache, access the network, or load the backend.
- Replaces direct FIL support with current nvForest model loading, CPU/GPU inference, model inspection, leaf IDs, per-tree predictions, and persistence. Random-forest inference and persistence use the same nvForest path.
- Corrects random-forest semantics: `mtry` controls predictors, `sample_fraction` controls rows, `trees` defaults to 100, `seed` reaches cuML, and prediction uses `type = "class"` or `type = "prob"`.
- Adds parsnip engines for `linear_reg()`, `logistic_reg()`, and `multinom_reg()` using `penalty` and `mixture`. Direct logistic regression adopts the same concepts and current iteration arguments. Linear models no longer emulate cuML's removed `normalize_input`; scaling belongs in preprocessing such as `recipes::step_normalize()`.
- Aligns prediction interfaces with R conventions: named prediction data is `new_data`, and KNN and classification probability prediction use `type` rather than bespoke flags.
- Versions portable model states with the package, schema, model ABI, and backend identity. Incompatible and unversioned states fail rather than migrate. Pointer-backed models support `bundle::bundle()` and `bundle::unbundle()`.
- Removes unsupported or obsolete interfaces: FIL, random projection, KNN IVFSQ, cuML log-level controls, `has_cuML()`, split cuML version queries, legacy serialization aliases, old logistic/SGD arguments, and historical prediction controls. IVFFlat and IVFPQ remain, including `n_bits` forwarding.
- Stops imposing an extra host-side TSVD sign convention. Tests compare mathematically equivalent decompositions without requiring signs to match another implementation.
- Raises the minimum R version to 4.1 because the new `bundle` dependency requires it.

## Backend, build, and runtime design

- Keeps only current RAPIDS 26.06 native APIs, requires the exact backend versions at configure and load time, and removes the historical version matrix, allocator shim, obsolete type aliases, fallback library names, and unavailable feature probes.
- Builds Treelite 4.7.0 and its exact locked source dependencies with the package compiler, default libstdc++ ABI, position-independent code, and OpenMP disabled. It links `libtreelite_static.a` privately and audits that neither Treelite symbols nor `libtreelite.so` enter the runtime ABI. Local functional builds must supply that same static-library contract.
- Excludes Treelite and its duplicate OpenMP runtime from the downloadable runtime. This resolves the Python wheel's incompatible C++ ABI while making XGBoost loading and random-forest persistence use one Treelite implementation.
- Includes the exact upstream licenses for Treelite and its source dependencies in the installed package. The package itself remains MIT licensed.
- Uses C++17, current RAFT resources, explicit stream-ordered copies, an out-of-tree CMake build, and generated native bindings. The managed fat binary contains SASS for compute capabilities 7.5, 8.0, 8.6, 8.9, 9.0, 10.0, and 12.0 plus PTX for 12.0.
- Uses one authoritative artifact lock for the build bootstrap and generated runtime manifest. Downloads use exact URLs, sizes, and SHA-256 hashes; build-only sources are excluded from the runtime manifest.
- Separates the shared runtime cache from package-specific backend DSOs. Reuse performs fast inventory checks; full hashing is reserved for `cuda_ml_runtime_audit()`. Publication is atomic under file locks, runtime RPATH/SONAME/NVRTC metadata is repaired, and package loading remains lazy.
- Ordinary source installs produce the explicit network-free CRAN/check stub. R-universe selects the managed functional build; local functional builds require `CUDA_ML_BUILD_MODE=local` and all exact inputs. Missing requirements do not silently turn a requested functional build into a stub.

## CI changes

- CRAN release and devel checks build the explicit stub and run under network isolation.
- The image build compiles and audits the backend without downloading and deleting the full runtime as a smoke test.
- The CPU runtime job installs once in the foreground, then uses fresh R processes to test loading, full audit, CPU nvForest inference, offline cache reuse, and NVRTC compilation without a GPU or system CUDA installation. This removes the previous concurrent `callr` installers whose undrained output pipes caused the 90-minute timeout.
- The GPU job installs once, runs a real K-means operation, and executes the full GPU test suite.

## Validation

- A clean CRAN-stub `R CMD build`, installation, and `R CMD check --no-manual --as-cran` pass. The local check reports only the host's missing optional `checkbashisms` executable and skips unavailable suggested packages `recipes` and `xgboost`.
- The full managed Docker image builds on Ubuntu 26.04 with GCC 15. It compiles the locked Treelite sources and native backend, then passes the dependency, architecture, registration, version, RPATH, and private-symbol audit.
- Isolated native probes load and serialize an XGBoost 3.2 UBJ model and import it into nvForest on CPU without the previous `std::bad_alloc` or serialization crash.
- Air formatting, R parsing, workflow YAML parsing, deterministic artifact/runtime lock generation, exact third-party license copies, `git diff --check`, and pkgdown site regeneration pass. Pkgdown reports the pre-existing missing alt text on the CRAN downloads badge.
- GitHub Actions passes the complete CRAN release/devel, managed-runtime CPU, and GPU paths on this head.

build and check {cuda.ml} in separate R sessions
description:
Fun story: when @dfalbel and I were working on https://github.com/mlverse/cuda.ml/pull/154, at one point when I tried installing {cuda.ml} with the pre-built version of `libcuml`, and then running `ldd libs/cuda.ml.so` from where {cuda.ml} was installed, I saw this type of output:

```
ldd cuda.ml.so
...
        libcuml++.so => /tmp/Rtmp<something>/<something>/libcuml++.so
...
```
which suggested to me the `libcuml++` shared library was not bundled quite correctly with the rest of the {cuda.ml} intallation. But oddly enough, everything in `r-cmd-check`, including the "installed package can be loaded from temporary location" check, came back OK. I later figured out that was only possible because the package installation and the checks were performed within the same R session. If the checks were done in a separate R session from the installation, then the `/tmp/Rtmp<something>/<something>/libcuml++.so` file would not have existed and the r-cmd-check would have surfaced the issue.

Also, it turns out for the linkage of `cuda.ml.so` to the bundled `libcuml++.so` to work in a *relocatable* manner (which is required for the package-loadable-from-temp-location check), `cuda.ml.so` must have its RPATH / RUNPATH set to '[$ORIGIN]'. This type of issue was again something that would have been surfaced if the package installation and r-cmd-check happened in separate R sessions, but would not have been surfaced otherwise.

Signed-off-by: Yitao Li <yitao@rstudio.com>

make 'CUDA_PATH' default to '/usr' with warning
description:
This change is made to accomodate (advanced) non-`conda` users.

Users who followed https://rapids.ai/start.html#get-rapids to install `cuML` through `conda` will see the `CUDA_PATH` env variable pointing to some valid location within their `rapids-<version>` conda env, and everything will work just fine without warning or error.

For other users, especially those who followed https://github.com/yitao-li/cuml-installation-notes#build-from-source-without-conda-and-without-multi-gpu-support or https://github.com/yitao-li/cuml-installation-notes#build-from-source-without-conda-and-with-multi-gpu-support, CUDA-related source code will only be compiled if `${CUDA_PATH}/include/cuml` is a directory. So for those users, it makes sense to assume `$CUDA_PATH` is `/usr` if it is not set. If the `cuML` libraries are installed at a non-standard location different from `/usr`, then users will need to set `$CUDA_PATH` explicitly for `cuml4r` to link with `cuML` libs successfully.

Signed-off-by: Yitao Li <yitao@rstudio.com>
